title: How to Export Graylog Logs
content_md: Graylog keeps its messages in OpenSearch or Elasticsearch, so you have two routes. Use the Graylog REST API, authenticated with an access token, or query the backend indices (graylog_* by default) directly with a script. Either way you get JSON. The original line is in message, and in full_message for some inputs. The export in the Graylog web interface produces a format LogTotal doesn’t read today. Graylog is a popular open log management platform, often the first central logging a team sets up. Prime Core has 23,274 detection rules for Graylog, mapped to 671 MITRE ATT&CK techniques. Below is how to get messages out, sanitize them, and investigate them for free in LogTotal. Get Started For Free Before you start An access token. In Graylog, open your user’s settings and create a token. With the API, you authenticate as :token: the token as the username and the word token as the password. Backend access, if you go direct. The OpenSearch or Elasticsearch cluster behind Graylog often isn’t reachable from outside. Ask whoever runs it for a read-only account. Streams and index sets. Graylog routes messages into streams, and streams map to index sets with their own prefixes and retention. Know which index set holds your data.
